s.t: Caroline Polachek and Teddy Geiger didn't know each other when her writing partner Dan Nigro brought Geiger in; they wrote it in six hours, mostly laughing on the floor.
s.src: PopCrush: Caroline Polachek on ‘So Hot You’re Hurting My Feelings’
s.q: Dan wanted to try seeing what it would be like to bring a third person into the studio, and I'm a fan of Teddy, just her whole wild energy, and she showed up. We didn't know each other at all, and we just spent six hours together writing this track, which most of it was just us laughing so hard that we were on the floor.

s.t: Caroline Polachek was surprised when TikTok users took up the dance from its video more than a year after its release, so she redid it herself ‘to close the loop’.
s.q: I was very surprised, because the track went viral on TikTok over a year after it came out as a single. ... I redid the dance myself on TikTok in order to close the loop.

s.t: Its bridge holds what Caroline Polachek calls the first guitar solo she had ever played with her voice.
s.src: PopCrush: Caroline Polachek on ‘So Hot You’re Hurting My Feelings’
s.q: the first guitar solo I've ever done with my voice

s.t: Caroline Polachek brought the title to the writing session: it was something she had said to someone weeks earlier, and she stuck with the idea.
s.src: PopCrush: Caroline Polachek on ‘So Hot You’re Hurting My Feelings’
s.q: I had that line actually before I even came into the session. It was something that I'd said to someone weeks prior, and I just kind of stuck with the idea.

s.t: A. G. Cook suggested the Christmas edit ‘So Cold You're Hurting My Feelings’, and Caroline Polachek has since sung its Christmas words on stage by mistake.
s.src: The Current: Caroline Polachek talks inspiration and new interpretations
s.q: for the PC Music Pop Carol Party he was like, 'Look, this is about as pop carol as we can get, why don't we do a Christmas edit of 'So Hot You're Hurting My Feelings.'' ... I've accidentally sung the Christmas lyrics on stage instead of the real lyrics.

f.t: She made the demo of Beyoncé's ‘No Angel’ at 5am in a London hotel room after a Chairlift show; Beyoncé later told her, ‘That beat was hot.’
f.src: The Telegraph (via Yahoo): Caroline Polachek: ‘Beyoncé told me: Girl, that beat is hot’
f.q: at 5am in a hotel room singing into a laptop after a Chairlift show in London ... "Girl, I didn't take any chances. That beat was hot."

f.t: As a teenager turned away from the Knitting Factory over a fake ID, she was sulking on the step when Mike Patton of Faith No More walked her in.
f.src: Far Out: The crazy encounter a young Caroline Polachek had with Mike Patton
f.q: Mike Patton actually personally walked me into a show at the Knitting Factory ... they weren't taking my fake ID and I couldn't get in. ... I was sitting, sulking on the front step ... I looked up to find Mike Patton looking at me saying, 'What's wrong?'

f.t: Hideo Kojima became a fan and posted about her on Instagram; she got in touch, they met in Paris, and she offered to write a song for Death Stranding 2.
f.src: The Line of Best Fit: Caroline Polachek debuts title track On The Beach
f.q: I was listening to Caroline Polachek last year and became a big fan. She contacted me after I posted about her on Instagram. We kept in touch, met up in Paris, and that's when she said she wanted to write a song for the game.

f.t: For her Ramona Lisa album Arcadia she sang straight into her laptop's built-in microphone, in hotel closets, quiet airport gates and spare dressing rooms on Chairlift's world tour.
f.q: She sang vocals directly into her computer's built in microphone, making use of hotel closets, quiet airport gates, and spare dressing rooms during Chairlift's world tour.

f.t: Studying fine art because music seemed ‘a pipe dream’, she had a job lined up as a gallery girl ‘out of pure pragmatism’.
f.src: The Telegraph (via Yahoo): Caroline Polachek: ‘Beyoncé told me: Girl, that beat is hot’
f.q: I even had a job lined up as a gallery girl, out of pure pragmatism.

nf.t: Written in six hours with a stranger, most of them spent laughing on the floor
